policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 1 Jun close (1x4 3.88, 3x6 3.98, 6x9 4.24, 9x12 4.45 vs WIBOR 3M 3.86) price roughly 60bp of NBP hikes within 12 months. The MPC held at 3.75% on 6 May; the 1-2 Jun meeting is expected to hold. PAP survey (1 Jun): a hold at 3.75% until Q3 2027; Glapiński (18 May): no commitments. May flash CPI 3.1% (29 May; 3.7% expected, -0.3% m/m on food); core 3.0% in April. The fuel VAT and excise cuts run to 15 June (extended 28 May).
policy.risk_text: May flash CPI 3.1% (3.7% expected) cut hike pricing sharply; the risks are the US-Iran memorandum failing (oil back above $100) and the end of the fuel package lifting CPI; long end: June supply (switch 3 Jun, sales 17 and 24 Jun) and a 6.5-7% deficit.

macro.projection_text: NBP March projection (4 Mar; data to 19 Feb, war excluded): CPI 50% bands 1.6-2.9% (2026), 1.1-3.7% (2027); central path 2.3% / 2.4% / 2.3% (2026-28), GDP 3.9% in 2026; IMF (14 Apr): 2026 CPI 3.3%; EC (21 May): GDP 3.5% in 2026. The July projection is the next marker.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit 7.3% of GDP (GUS EDP, 22 Apr), debt 59.7%; 2026 deficit cap PLN 271.7bn; budget deficit after April PLN 89.3bn (30.1% of the limit); the government's assumptions put the 2026 deficit at ~6.8% of GDP; EC (21 May): 6.5%, debt 64.5%; windfall-tax bill (75% of margins above the 2025 level +20%) in preparation; fuel package (VAT 8%, price caps, minimum excise) to 15 June (28 May).
macro.fiscal_risk_text: 2026 needs ~56% (MoF, 29 May) financed; budget accounts >PLN 200bn expected at end-May (Drop, 29 May). S&P affirmed A-/stable (8 May) and its analyst calls the missing medium-term consolidation the key rating risk (26 May); Scope A negative (15 May); Fitch A- and Moody's A2 have negative outlooks.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP has held at 3.75% since the 4 Mar cut (next MPC 1-2 Jun); May CPI 3.1% y/y; Q1 GDP 3.5% y/y (second estimate). Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 1 Jun: Q1 GDP revised to 3.5% y/y (flash 3.4), but consumption (3.3%) and investment (2.4%) missed forecasts; May PMI rose to 49.4 (48.5 expected). MoF offers OK0129, NZ0331, PS0731, DS1034, DS0436 and NZ0936 at the 3 Jun switch, buying back DS0726, PS1026, WZ1126, OK0127, PS0527. PAP survey: hold at 3.75% until Q3 2027. Yields rose on US-Iran setbacks; PKO sees the 10Y below 5.60% by week-end. Abroad: after weekend US-Iran exchanges of fire, Iran halted talks via mediators over Israel's strikes in Lebanon and threatened to fully close Hormuz; Brent (Aug) jumped up to 7% to ~$96-97, TTF +6% to EUR49; UST10 4.50%, Bund 10Y 3.00% (+7bp). >90% priced for a June ECB hike, ~two BoE hikes, >60% for a December Fed hike; ISM manufacturing 54.0. Trump later said Israel and Hezbollah agreed to halt attacks.

calendar.plan_text: MoF June plan (29 May): one switch on 3 Jun (settles 8 Jun; buys back DS0726, PS1026, WZ1126, OK0127, PS0527) and sale auctions on 17 and 24 Jun (PLN 6-12bn each) in OK0129, NZ0331, PS0731, DS0436 and NZ0936; no T-bills; ~56% of 2026 needs financed. 3 Jun switch offer (1 Jun): sells OK0129, NZ0331, PS0731, DS1034, DS0436 and NZ0936. BGK: FPC switch on 18 Jun (buys back FPC0427).
calendar.timing_text: The Aug 2025-Feb 2026 pattern (auction-day close the cheapest point of the week) comes from a rally regime; March's sell-off broke it and April's auction days cheapened on average. Remaining June operations: 3 Jun (switch), 17 Jun, 24 Jun. MPC 1-2 Jun: a hold is expected.

core_text: Regime: talks stalled and Gulf clashes resumed - Brent back at ~$95-98; the NBP is at 3.75% while FRAs price roughly 60bp of NBP hikes; the ECB is priced for a June hike, the Fed is priced for a 2026 hike, the BoE is priced for hikes, the CNB is on hold and the MNB is on hold. Poland's 5Y CDS was 51bp and the 10Y spread to Bunds 271bp on benchmark bonds (Erste, 1 Jun close). Iran halts talks; Brent +6% to ~$96 (1 Jun).
